messages:
alex: quick share — profiler shows the new prefix coalescer holding a kernel latch during warmup; observed repeated small batches that prevent KV prefill from completing. GPU slab fragmentation creeps up and TTL-driven evictions spike around 120s. cc @maria @sanjay

maria: can you paste the profiler snippet and the numbers?

alex: attaching quick dump:
```
timeline: warmup 0-180s
- coalescer_lock_hold: 42ms avg (spikes 120ms)
- small_batch_ratio: 68% (<=8 token batches)
- kv_prefill_progress: stalls at 23% until coalescer unlock
- gpu_slab_frag: +12% over baseline
- ttl_evictions/sec: baseline 4 -> 29 at 120s
```

perf-bot: auto-metric: p95_lat +18% at 2954600060, cache_hitrate -2.4%

sanjay: hmm, binder path seems to be holding the kernel slot while trying to merge prefixes. Is this the new "aggressive_coalesce" flag?

alex: yes, `kv.coalesce_mode=aggressive` on canary. config: `kv.coalesce_threshold_ms=12` and `batch_hysteresis_ms=10` in the canary.

julia: that hysteresis looks high for our traffic pattern. most requests are short; hysteresis keeps kernels open waiting for more inflight. proposal: drop to `4ms` and add an early-exit when small_batch_ratio>0.6.

kevin: pushed a tiny change to reduce lock granularity (PR #8421) — changes: hold coalescer_lock only for prefix-lookup, not KV insertion. Rolling to 5% canary now.

maria: canary conditions: abort if `gpu_slab_frag` > 20% OR `ttl_evictions/sec` > baseline*5 OR `cache_hitrate` drops > 3% within 5m. also watch p95 and tail memory OOMs.

perf-bot: canary @5% metrics snapshot (2954600090):
- p50 +0.9%
- p95 +3.1%
- cache_hitrate -0.9%
- ttl_evictions/sec +9
- gpu_slab_frag +3%
- OOM_count 0

sanjay: numbers look acceptable so far. still want to avoid long-lived bucket locks. alex can you instrument `coalescer_lock_hold` histogram and add per-kernel-owner tags?

alex: yes will add histogram and owner tag (`owner=coalescer|prefill|kernel`) and push to canary. also toggling `kv.coalesce_threshold_ms` to 6 in a second experiment to see warmup throughput.

julia: can we also tweak TTL ramping? idea: stagger TTL eviction windows during warmup to avoid mass evictions when prefill finally completes. e.g., add jitter to TTL sweep start times per slab.

kevin: added jitter to TTL sweep in branch — default is `ttl_sweep_jitter_ms=0`, experiment set to `2500ms`.

maria: ops runbook: if OOM_count >0 or slab_frag increases >15% in 10m, rollback. if cache_hitrate drops >3% for 10m, rollback. otherwise keep canary for 2h and gather histograms.

perf-bot: updated canary snapshot (2954600120): p95 +1.8%, cache_hitrate -0.3%, ttl_evictions/sec +4, gpu_slab_frag +1%, OOM_count 0

alex: good — keeping the experiment open for 2h. next steps: (1) add lock-hold histogram + owner tag, (2) run `kv.coalesce_threshold_ms=6` vs `4` A/B, (3) TTL sweep jitter retention test. will post results here.

maria: thanks. leaving a note to link the flamegraphs and perf dashboards once available. :thumbsup:
